Simple setup

The shortest path for vibe coders: install Flisk, let it check your machine, clone a working stack, and run it.

Start here

Copy five commands. Get a real local stack.

Do this first. Come back for manual binaries, licenses, and from-scratch service wiring after you have seen Flisk boot once.

  1. 1 Install
  2. 2 Check
  3. 3 Clone example
  4. 4 Run

Coming from the old package? The CLI used to ship as @tdk-landscape/tdk-cli-core, and that package still owns the tdk command on your machine. Remove it once, then install Flisk: npm uninstall -g @tdk-landscape/tdk-cli-core && npm install -g @flisk-sh/flisk. Without that, npm stops with EEXIST: file already exists and the flisk command never lands on your PATH. The curl installer above has no such conflict: it writes flisk directly.

Simple setup

If you already have Docker running, this is the whole happy path.

terminal
curl -fsSL https://flisk.sh/install.sh | sh
flisk doctor
flisk project example
cd tdk-example
flisk up
01

Install the CLI

The installer picks the right public binary for macOS or Linux, Intel or Arm.

02

Run doctor

Flisk tells you what is missing before it tries to boot Docker, Tilt, or generated config.

03

Use the example

Start from a working PSR landscape instead of inventing the folder structure cold.

04

Boot the stack

flisk up generates the local files and hands orchestration to Tilt.

Before you run it

Flisk needs a container runtime and Tilt. Node.js is only needed when your project has frontend tooling.

  • Docker installed and running
  • Tilt installed
  • Node.js 18+ for frontend stacks

Install options

Use curl if you just want the fastest install. Use npm, npx, pnpm, or bun if you prefer package-manager workflows.

terminal
curl -fsSL https://flisk.sh/install.sh | sh
npm install -g @flisk-sh/flisk
# run without installing globally
npx @flisk-sh/flisk --version

# or scaffold a project directly
npx @flisk-sh/flisk project --yes
pnpm add -g @flisk-sh/flisk
bun add -g @flisk-sh/flisk

Verify installation

terminal
flisk --version
# prints the installed version, e.g. 1.3.74

Add your license (if using premium features)

The free tier requires no license key. Premium and Enterprise keys unlock extras such as Verdaccio private registry, Playwright E2E, C4 diagrams, and structured logging.

Have a Premium or Enterprise key?

Export it before running flisk up. Flisk checks the key automatically on the next run.

terminal
export TDK_LICENSE_KEY=tdk-xxxxxx

Add that line to ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc if you want it to persist. Each key covers up to 100 distinct projects, unlimited on Enterprise. If the key is missing, expired, or unreachable, Flisk keeps running with the free engine.

What actually happens when you run it

Before Tilt touches Docker, flisk checks your environment and tells you exactly what it's doing — no guessing what's happening behind the spinner.

zsh: flisk doctor && flisk up

Don't have Docker or Tilt yet?

flisk up won't just fail silently — it checks both before touching anything, and tells you precisely what's missing and how to fix it:

terminal
$ flisk up

Flisk can't start - missing prerequisites:

❌ Docker (or a compatible container runtime) is not running

💡 Suggestions:
   → Start Docker Desktop, then verify with: `docker ps`
   → Or start Colima: `colima start`
   → Or start the Docker service on Linux: `sudo systemctl start docker`
   → Setup guide: https://flisk.sh/docs/quickstart/

❌ Tilt CLI is not installed

💡 Suggestions:
   → Install Tilt: `brew install tilt` (macOS)
   → Or download from: https://docs.tilt.dev/install.html
   → Verify with: `tilt version`

Run `flisk doctor` for a full environment check.

Fix what it flags, run flisk doctor to confirm, and you're clear to boot.

Start from a working example

Not sure what a Flisk project should look like yet? Skip the blank canvas. flisk project <template> clones a complete PSR landscape you can run immediately.

terminal
# minimal reference stack - start here if you're new to Flisk
flisk project example

# or a fuller domain example
flisk project restaurant
flisk project user-management
flisk project erp

cd <cloned-folder>
flisk doctor   # check Docker/Tilt are ready
flisk up       # start the stack

Use --path <dir> to control the destination folder name. See Examples for what each template contains.

Success

Your stack is now running locally. Every new teammate who clones the repo gets the same result in minutes, not weeks.

Build from scratch

After the example makes sense, create a blank project and add your first backend resource.

terminal
mkdir my-service
cd my-service
flisk project --yes
flisk resource api --type backend --stack pre-alpha --path services/pre-alpha/api
flisk project --check
flisk up pre-alpha

Flisk validates .tdk/project.json, generates files in .tdk/.tdk-out/, and reads boot order from each resource's dependsOn list.

Manual binary download

Download a binary from the public release repo if you prefer to install it yourself.

terminal
curl -fsSL -o flisk https://github.com/flisk-sh/releases/releases/latest/download/tdk-linux-amd64
chmod +x flisk
sudo mv flisk /usr/local/bin/flisk

Binaries ship from flisk-sh/releases.

Try Flisk with Docker Compose

Use Docker Compose if you want to try Flisk without installing the binary on your host.

terminal
git clone https://github.com/flisk-sh/tdk-docker-compose-example.git
cd tdk-docker-compose-example
docker compose run --rm flisk flisk --version
docker compose run --rm flisk flisk project --yes
